extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (authors and reviewers) submitting to or using the F1000Research platform
extracted.subtask_description: Platform-specific policies and quality standards for publishing, versioning, open peer review, data deposition, indexing and related procedures on F1000Research. Intended to guide authors, reviewers and editors in preparing, submitting, reviewing and citing work on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication before peer review (not a preprint server)
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles in F1000Research are permanently published (with a DOI) and undergo formal peer review after publication. Since peer review starts the moment they are published, they are NOT preprints and cannot be submitted to other journals, regardless of the peer review outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under rare circumstances peer review may be discontinued and the article labelled accordingly; in those cases authors may submit the article to another journal but must discuss this with the F1000Research team first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review status is displayed on articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review status is displayed in the upper right-hand corner of articles and appended to the article title (e.g. AWAITING PEER REVIEW). As peer review reports are published the approval status is updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediately on publication an article is labelled AWAITING PEER REVIEW until the first peer review report is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which content types are peer reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles published on F1000Research undergo peer review, with the exception of editorials which are typically commissioned. Posters, slides and documents are not peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters and slides are clearly labelled as not peer reviewed; documents undergo a basic screen only.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house editorial checks before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are checked by the in-house editorial team to ensure each submission is (co-)authored by a qualified researcher or clinician and is appropriate in terms of content, quality, tone and format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks include completeness, absence of plagiarism, meeting ethical standards, citations to supporting data, adequate methods/protocol information, understandable writing, and compliance with article guidelines. Posters and slides receive a briefer topical appropriateness check before receiving an identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of 'sound science'
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for F1000Research is to publish 'sound science'. Articles that the in-house team and advisors consider not to be sound science are not accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after publication reviewers may judge a published article to not be sound science; authors are encouraged to submit revised versions addressing criticisms. On rare occasions papers may be unanimously negatively reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of reviewer approval statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign statuses: 'Approved' (technically sound; no or only minor revisions), 'Approved with Reservations' (reviewer believes paper has academic merit but has asked for a number of small changes or sometimes more significant revisions), and 'Not Approved' (current version not of high enough standard; flaws that undermine results/conclusions unless fixed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statuses are deliberately distinct from traditional journal decisions (Accepted/Minor/Major Revisions/Rejected). The definition of 'Approved with Reservations' was revised in June 2020 to clarify its scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing criteria based on peer review statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: An article will be indexed in bibliographic databases once it receives two 'Approved' statuses, or two 'Approved with Reservations' statuses and one 'Approved' status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing rules have changed historically (e.g., during beta and at formal launch in 2013); authors should refer to current statements on indexing for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review: reviewers named and reports published
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research names reviewers and publishes their reports alongside the article; everyone can see reviewer names and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: reduces bias, gives reviewers credit, improves report quality, and offers informative critiques to readers. Published evidence (randomized controlled trials) is cited showing signed reports are often more constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are formally invited by F1000Research; the editorial team primarily identifies suitable reviewers but authors may suggest reviewers (all suggestions are checked before invitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective reviewers who have collaborated or are currently collaborating with any of the authors are not eligible to review. Reviewers are also asked to declare any competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial administration of reviewer contact
rubrics_metrics.description: The F1000Research team administers the peer-review process and contacts reviewers on behalf of authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked not to contact reviewers directly as this can influence objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring competing interests for reviewers and commenters
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and anyone commenting are asked to declare any competing interests, along with full name and affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration of interests is required to ensure transparency of potential biases for reviewers and commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of peer review for lack of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose articles have 0 reports after 6 months, or only 1 report after 9 months, may choose to discontinue peer review in consultation with the F1000Research team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When peer review is discontinued a notice is added to the Open Peer Review box; such articles are not indexed in PubMed and may be considered equivalent to a preprint. Authors wishing to submit elsewhere must notify F1000Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning: revisions and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can publish new versions of their article at any time. New versions addressing peer review are 'Revised'; small developments or additional information after peer review are 'Updates'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised versions are published free of charge; a small APC is charged for updated versions (as of May 2019). When a new version is published, reviewers of the previous version are invited to re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges: '[Revised]' vs '[Update]'
rubrics_metrics.description: '[Revised]' indicates a new version usually incorporating changes in response to reviewers' comments; '[Update]' indicates a new version adding small developments, often after indexing/peer review is considered complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges distinguish types of new versions to clarify the nature of changes between versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship changes across versions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author list changes in a new version of the same article, the new version can be published with an explanation included in the 'Amendments' section at the top of the new version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each version has its own DOI so citation is version-specific. Any changes in authorship must be confirmed by all authors in writing or by email; the corresponding author is responsible for obtaining confirmation. F1000Research may contact co-authors directly to confirm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and retraction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Once published on F1000Research an article cannot be withdrawn because it has a DOI and must be permanently retained. Serious issues may lead to retraction and an explanatory note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If peer review is discontinued, the article remains published but labelled; authors wishing to submit elsewhere must contact the editorial team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to deposit all underlying data associated with an article in an approved repository so other researchers can analyze and try to reproduce results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject-specific repositories exist (e.g., PDB), authors should deposit there. See data preparation guidelines for acceptable repositories and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of data required
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be enough data provided that another researcher could reanalyse and/or try to reproduce the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amount required depends on experiment types; authors unsure about sufficiency should contact the editorial team for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive/patient data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If data cannot be adequately anonymized to address security or patient confidentiality, it can usually be stored in an access-controlled database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases all researchers who meet necessary criteria must be given access to review the data on request; HIPAA de-identification standards are referenced as an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended data license
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research recommends the use of the CC0 (Creative Commons Public Domain Dedication) license for datasets associated with articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recommendation to maximize reuse; repository policies and funder mandates may also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format includes version and peer review status
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations for F1000Research articles include the article version number and the number of peer review reports that have received 'Approved', 'Approved with Reservations' or 'Not Approved' statuses, placed in square brackets after the article title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided: Authors. Article title [version number; details of peer review status]. F1000Research YEAR, volume:publication number (doi). Use the Cite button on article pages for formatted citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review reports are citable and have DOIs
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review reports associated with F1000Research articles are assigned a DOI on publication and can be cited independently from the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided for citing a peer review report; each report includes a 'Copyright information' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article-level metrics and impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research provides article-level metrics such as Altmetrics, Scopus and PubMed citations (for indexed articles), and counts of views and PDF downloads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform emphasizes article-level assessment over journal-level metrics (no Impact Factor), and encourages assessing individual articles on their merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: APC policy: waivers, discounts, charges and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting authors with primary affiliation in World Bank-defined low-income economies are entitled to 100% APC waiver; a 50% discount is available to authors from certain lower-middle income economies with GDP < $200B. Revised versions are free; updated versions incur a small APC (as of May 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No APC refunds are offered if an article is not indexed or receives no reviewers; F1000Research states APCs cover publication and support costs. Details of fees are linked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and backup strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles that pass peer review are archived in PubMed Central and the British Library; all articles at any stage are indexed by Portico. Data and code are stored only in approved repositories with acceptable archiving policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to ensure long-term preservation; authors should deposit data in repositories approved by F1000Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses and copyright for articles and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research articles are usually published under a CC-BY license. Peer review reports are published under CC-BY. Copyright remains with the current copyright holder (usually the author or reviewer or their institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some waivers or alternate arrangements may apply for certain governmental employees; copyright information is shown below the abstract or alongside reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments policy and moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolicited open scientific discussion on articles is encouraged via the Comment system; commenters must declare competing interests and provide full name/affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abusive behavior is not tolerated; extreme cases may result in contacting the affiliated institution or other actions. Comments are published according to policies linked on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies for posters and slides
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research publishes academic posters and slides within gateways/collections only. They are labelled as not peer reviewed and are initially published without a DOI until a quick internal editorial check is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters/slides can be uploaded even if already on other sites (multiple DOIs possible). Abstracts for posters should be short summaries, not reuse of copyrighted conference abstracts. Most posters/slides are published under CC-BY but specific licenses may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion guidance before peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid promoting articles in the media until the article has passed the open peer review process. Social media promotion is encouraged once the article is published; include the full citation with peer review status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The citation includes approval status to make the peer review stage clear to readers and media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers receive 20% off the article processing charge for one article if submitted and published in the 12 months following submission of their peer review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an incentive to recognize reviewing contribution; further details available from the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID integration for authors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting authors are required to connect their ORCID iD at submission; when the work is published all co-authors are sent a link to connect their iD. Peer review reports can be added to ORCID profiles to give reviewers credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once connected, works published with the author named will automatically be added to their ORCID account; F1000Research has worked with ORCID and CASRAI for integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform scope and accepted article types
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research publishes a wide range of research outputs across life and physical sciences, engineering, medicine, social sciences and humanities, including research articles, brief reports, reviews, systematic reviews, opinion, correspondence, data notes, case reports, clinical practice papers, protocols, methods, observation, antibody validation, and software tool articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform welcomes positive, negative or null studies, replication studies and refutation studies equally; detailed descriptions of each article type are in the article guidelines.
